## Problem 1

Annotation to the code was improved and adjusted

```{r}
#Import packages
library(deSolve)
library(ggplot2)


#define a function that replicates the mathematical equations
TI.model <- function(t, x, parms) {
  Ta <- x[1] # pop 1
  I  <- x[2] # pop 2
  with(as.list(parms),{
    dT <- lambda- deltaT * Ta - beta * Ta * I #changes in pops
    dI <- beta * Ta * I - deltaI * I #changes in pop
    res <- c(dT, dI)
    list(res)
  })
}

# define the parameters of for the function
parmsTI  <- c(lambda = 1000, 
               deltaT = 0.05,
               deltaI = log(2)/1.39,
               beta = NA)

parmsTI["beta"] <- 5/(parmsTI["lambda"]/parmsTI["deltaT"]/parmsTI["deltaI"]) #write beta as a function of R0 and the other parameters

#define the starting T population. 
xstartTI <- c(Ta = as.numeric(parmsTI["lambda"]/parmsTI["deltaT"]), 
               I = 1) 
#define a time vector
times  <- seq(0, 100, length=500)

#here rk4 is a function provided by R to solve differential equations which you do not have to understand in further detail
out.TI <- as.data.frame(rk4(xstartTI, times, TI.model, parmsTI))

out.TI_long = out.TI |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols= -time) 

#plotting of the numerically solved quantities
#fill in the gaps by yourself
ggplot(data =  out.TI_long, mapping= aes(x = time, y = value, color = name)) +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  theme_classic() 



```

ui <- fluidPage(
  
  titlePanel("Varying lambda in the TI model"),
  sidebarLayout(
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("lambda", "value of lambda", min = 0, max = 2000, value = 1000),
    sliderInput("deltaT", "value deltaT", min = 0, max = 1, value = 0.05, step = 0.01),
    sliderInput("deltaI", "value deltaI", min = 0, max = 1, value = 0.5, step = 0.01),
    sliderInput("beta", "value beta", min = 0, max = 0.01, value = 0.001, step = 0.0001)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("plot")
  )))
  


server <- function(input, output){
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    
    parmsTI2  <- c(lambda = input$lambda, 
               deltaT = input$deltaT,
               deltaI = input$deltaI,
               beta = input$beta)
    
    xstartTI2 <- c(Ta = as.numeric(2000), I = 1)
    
    times2  <- seq(0, 100, length = 500)
    

    #perform calculation
    out.TI2 <- as.data.frame(rk4(xstartTI2, times2, TI.model, parmsTI2))
    
    out.TI_long2 = out.TI2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols= -time)
    
#plot the result
    ggplot(data =  out.TI_long2, mapping= aes(x = time, y = value, color = name)) +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  theme_classic() 

  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Problem 2 - Exercise c 

Calculate the parameters for rate I

```{r}
#import data
virusLoad <- read_csv("Content_per_day/Day_two_content/Exercises Olat Upload/data/virusLoadOnTreatment.csv")

ggplot(virusLoad, aes(x = time, y = V)) +
  geom_point()



getSSG <- function(parm){
  Io_fi <- parm[1]
  deltaI <- parm[2]
  
  I_fit <- Io_fi * exp((-deltaI) * virusLoad$time)
  SSQ <- (log(I_fit) - log(virusLoad$V))**2
  
  return(sum(SSQ))

}

I0_fit <- optim(par = c(1, 1), fn = getSSG)$par[1]
deltaI_fit <- optim(par = c(1,1), fn = getSSG)$par[2]



ggplot(virusLoad, aes(x = time, y = log(V))) +
  geom_point()

model <- lm(log(V) ~ time, virusLoad)
deltaI_est <- summary(model)["coefficients"][[1]][1]


#calculate t1/2



#t1/2 
t1_2 <- log(1/2)/(deltaI_fit)

```
